verification.source: Cross-checked across TaxTips.ca, catax.tools, and targeted searches for CPP2/QPP/QPIP/EI figures; not fetched directly from CRA.ca or any provincial finance ministry. Needs a primary-source pass on every figure before `--strict` will accept `verified`. See per-section notes below for which specific figures carry extra uncertainty.
verification.note: Single-file layout (all 13 provinces/territories + federal + CPP + EI in one JSON, one fetch), unlike the US convention of 51 lazy-fetched per-state files - deliberate for Canada given only 13 jurisdictions, no need for the lazy-load complexity that scale justifies for the US.

notes: Canada's Basic Personal Amount (federal AND provincial) is a NON-REFUNDABLE TAX CREDIT, not a pre-bracket deduction the way the UK Personal Allowance or US standard deduction are - see ca-engine.js header comment for why this changes the arithmetic.

federal.basicPersonalAmount.taper models the BPA phasing down to a NON-ZERO FLOOR (14,829 of 16,452), unlike the UK Personal Allowance which tapers to zero. `calculateTaperedAllowance`'s optional `floor` parameter exists specifically for this.
Provincial/territorial Basic Personal Amounts are modelled as flat (no income-tested taper) for all 13 jurisdictions - a documented V1 simplification, not a confirmed fact that none of them taper.

Quebec (`provinces.QC`) is not just another province row: it carries its own `qpp` (replaces `cpp`), `eiReduced` (replaces `ei`'s rate, same national maxInsurableEarnings), `qpip` (an additional premium with no non-Quebec equivalent), and `quebecAbatementRate` (reduces FEDERAL tax owing, not provincial). See ca-engine.js's `isQuebec` branch.

Two aggregator sources disagreed on the 4th-bracket rate: 29.0% vs 29.29%/29.31% (the latter alongside a capital-gains table, likely a mid-2025 transition artifact, not a 2026 full-year rate). 29% was chosen as the more likely stable figure - needs direct CRA.ca confirmation.
reducedByDollarOver is derived: (16452 - 14829) / (258482 - 181440) = 1623 / 77042 = 0.0210664, i.e. the BPA loses about 2.1 cents per dollar of income in the phase-out range.
Employee-only rates. Employer share is not a deduction from employee pay and is not modelled.

CPP2 (the second, additional tier) is a distinct mechanic added in 2024 with no UK/US equivalent - a separate contribution on a separate earnings range (base ceiling to secondTier ceiling), not another band on the base schedule.

The 2026 YMPE/YAMPE (74,600 / 85,000) are INFERRED from Quebec's confirmed 2026 QPP ceilings, not independently sourced for CPP directly - CPP's YMPE and QPP's MPE are set by the same national calculation and have historically matched exactly, but this needs direct confirmation.
The $3,500 basic exemption is a flat, historically unindexed figure - unlike almost every other threshold here, it does not rise annually.
Applies to every province/territory EXCEPT Quebec, which uses `provinces.QC.eiReduced` instead (same maxInsurableEarnings, lower rate, because QPIP covers what EI would otherwise fund federally).

AB.name: Alberta
notes: No surtax, no health premium - the default province for Canada mode precisely because it has none of the wrinkles Ontario/Quebec do.

BC.name: British Columbia
notes: 7 brackets - the most of any non-Quebec province other than Newfoundland & Labrador.

NL.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
notes: 8 brackets - the most of any jurisdiction in this dataset, federal included.

ON.name: Ontario
notes: Most complex non-Quebec province - surtax AND health premium both apply.

Health premium plateau values ($0/$300/$450/$600/$750/$900) and the $20,000/$36,000/$48,000 boundaries were confirmed via search; the finer ramp thresholds (approx. 25,000/38,500/48,600/72,600/200,600) were NOT independently re-confirmed and are reconstructed from the well-documented general shape of the Ontario Health Premium - needs a primary-source pass against the T4032-ON table.

Surtax is a tax-on-a-tax: a percentage of PROVINCIAL TAX OWING (after the provincial BPA credit), not of income. Both tiers are additive - above the second threshold, the 20% and 36% surtax both apply simultaneously.

Health premium is a step function of taxable income (flat dollar amounts, ramping between plateaus): each step's `upTo` is where the NEXT ramp begins, and the step's `cap` naturally holds the premium flat for the rest of that range, so a 'ramp then plateau' shape is one step, not two.

PE.name: Prince Edward Island
notes: PEI's surtax was discontinued in 2024. An earlier research pass found one aggregator source that incorrectly still listed a surtax; a second, more specific search confirmed it no longer applies. `surtax: null` is a deliberate, confirmed omission, not an oversight.

QC.name: Quebec
notes: Not just a different bracket table: a different pension plan (qpp), a different (reduced) EI rate, an additional QPIP premium, and a federal tax abatement. See ca-engine.js's `isQuebec` branch.
Quebec residents are NOT charged CPP - `qpp` replaces `cpp` entirely for this province.

eiReduced uses the SAME national maxInsurableEarnings as `ei` (68,900) - only the rate differs (1.30% vs 1.66%). An earlier draft incorrectly modelled a separate, lower ceiling for Quebec; corrected after re-reading the source.
qpip is a SEPARATE premium on top of (not instead of) eiReduced, with its own much higher maxInsurableEarnings (103,000).
quebecAbatementRate (16.5%) reduces FEDERAL tax owing, not provincial - see the top-level `federal` section and ca-engine.js's `abatement` calculation.

QPP rate re-checked with a second, more targeted search after an earlier pass misread a combined employee+employer figure (10.6%) as employee-only. Correct 2026 employee-only figures: 5.3% base + 1.0% first additional = 6.3% combined (modelled as one `base.rate`), plus 4.0% QPP2 on 74,600-85,000.

YT.name: Yukon
notes: First three bracket thresholds mirror the federal thresholds exactly - a real design choice by Yukon, not a data-entry error.

NU.name: Nunavut
notes: Lowest marginal rates of any jurisdiction in this dataset - 4% starting bracket.
